summary:
CropSense is a mobile and web app that helps Indian farmers choose what to sow using NASA Earth data and their own soil evidence. Farmers map a field on satellite imagery, add Soil Health Card values and simple field observations, then get explained crop suitability and three-season rotation plans—not opaque yield promises.

It addresses the challenge of turning Earth observations into practical farm decisions. CropSense pulls climate and moisture from NASA POWER, greenness from MODIS NDVI, mapped soil from SoilGrids, and climate outlook from CMIP6, then combines those with local soil tests. Advice is multilingual, transparent about sources, and framed for discussion with a Krishi Vigyan Kendra.

It matters because many smallholders face uncertain rain, limited irrigation, and conflicting advice. CropSense puts satellite intelligence and farmer knowledge in one place so crop choices better match soil, water, and season—reducing risk while keeping farmers in control.
details:
CropSense turns a farmer’s mapped field into practical crop-rotation guidance using NASA and open Earth data—so smallholders get field-specific advice instead of generic calendars.

What it does / how it works

A farmer signs in, maps a field boundary, and optionally adds soil-test details. CropSense then pulls live Earth observations for that location—NASA POWER (moisture, rainfall, temperature extremes), MODIS NDVI (crop greenness), SoilGrids (texture/pH), and Open-Meteo climate outlooks—and combines them with local crop rules to recommend a three-crop rotation plan with clear “why” explanations. It works as a mobile app (Expo) for use in the field and a desktop web app for planning and review.

Benefits

- Field-specific advice instead of one-size-fits-all crop lists

- Uses free public satellite/climate data—no expensive sensors required

- Helps improve soil health, reduce water stress, and diversify planting risk

- Simple, multilingual interface designed for real farm workflows

- Transparent sources so farmers can trust where the numbers come from

Intended impact

Help Indian (and similar) smallholder farmers make better rotation decisions that protect soil, conserve water, and improve resilience to climate stress—while making NASA Earth science usable at the village level.

Tools, languages, hardware, software

-Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript

-Mobile:React Native, Expo

Web: React, Vite, React Router, Leaflet / react-leaflet

- Data / APIs: NASA POWER, MODIS (ORNL DAAC), ISRIC SoilGrids, Open-Meteo

- Backend / auth:** Supabase Auth + Postgres (`account_farm_records`)

- Other:** Turf.js (field geometry), TanStack Query, Lucide icons

- Hardware:Standard smartphones and laptops/desktops (no custom hardware)

- Hosting: AntiDeploy (`https://cropsense.antideploy.app`)

How it’s creative

CropSense doesn’t stop at showing satellite maps—it translates NASA POWER, MODIS, and SoilGrids into a farmer-facing rotation plan with plain-language reasons. It bridges Earth observation and agriculture by fusing multiple open datasets into one decision workflow, with both phone and desktop experiences so advice is useful in the field and for longer planning sessions.

Factors the team considered

- Farmer trust (show data sources; decision support, not yield guarantees)

- Offline/poor-connectivity realities and simple Farmer ID onboarding

- Language accessibility (e.g. English/Hindi)

- Accuracy vs. usability (global grids vs. local soil tests—farmer input can override mapped soil)

- Water stress and climate risk, not only yield

- Privacy and secure account storage for farm records

- Cross-platform access: phone for mapping, web for deeper review
